action: Instruct patient: 'Press out your body to make a round tummy.'
interpretation: Use the distended abdomen maneuver to displace bowel gas and optimize the acoustic window.

action: Scan the epigastric region in the transverse plane. Identify anatomical landmarks surrounding the pancreas.
interpretation: Visualize the stomach, the left liver lobe, the right liver lobe, and the interlobal fissure.

action: Focus scanning attention immediately posterior to the stomach.
interpretation: Identify the structure located right behind the stomach as the pancreas body.

action: Position the probe transversely. Observe the anatomy, then slide the probe slightly to the patient's right side and downwards.
interpretation: Visualize the pancreas tail extending posteriorly ('going back') and the pancreas body anteriorly ('in the front'). Upon moving right and down, identify the pancreas head.

action: Locate the 'leading structure' for the pancreas by tracing the vascular landmarks. Follow the veins to the center of the liver.
interpretation: Identify the splenic vein coming from the back joining the mesenteric vein (coming from the caudal part) to produce the portal vein. Use the splenic vein as the primary landmark.

action: Rotate the probe 90 degrees into a longitudinal (sagittal) position.
interpretation: Evaluate the pancreas in cross-section (seen as a long section relative to the body axis).

action: Maintain the longitudinal probe position and look posterior to the stomach.
interpretation: Visualize the pancreas body situated right behind the stomach.

action: Slide the probe further to the patient's right side while maintaining the longitudinal plane.
interpretation: Locate and visualize the pancreas head in this region.

action: Slide the probe to the patient's left side. Trace the vascular structures posteriorly.
interpretation: Visualize the splenic vein and the splenic artery (positioned cranial to the vein) extending back. Confirm the pancreas tail follows these vessels back to the 'spleen helix'.

action: If stomach gas obscures the view of the pancreas body and tail, reposition the probe to use a 'splenic window' (left lateral approach). Search for the splenic vein.
interpretation: Attempt to find the splenic vein through the splenic window and look for the structure located immediately caudal to it.
Stabilize the image to reduce respiratory motion.
Allow patient to relax before the next breath hold.
Freeze respiration to capture the view through the splenic window.

action: Scan immediately caudal to the splenic vein.
interpretation: Identify the structure caudal to the vein as the pancreas tail, extending right to the 'splenic helix'.
